prior_summary: Role-factored relative geometry: a shared encoder processes both pose-and-goal bundles using world and TCP-relative translations, relative rotations, goal errors and causal differences. Learned latent-role attention pools object interactions; a separate fixed-base robot stream conditions a learned action DDPM. This is a representation-sharing prior, not a phase controller.
applicable_conditions: Same Panda and joint-target controller, state observations in world metres with wxyz quaternions, accessible top-down 0.04 m cubes, and the demonstrated red-first then blue ordering. Supports initial open-gripper acquisition, partial selected-block approach/closure/lift, and incoming red lowering/release/retreat before blue acquisition. The executable interface has no external intended-object token: intent must be consistent with the demonstrated causal scene context and cannot be independently commanded through forward.
termination_guidance: A useful delivery handoff has the selected cube elevated and co-moving with the near-downward TCP, closed-finger state around 0.0183 m per finger, and initial goalward translation while retaining the demonstrated -1 gripper command. Observed endpoints are approximately red z 0.280-0.283 m and blue z 0.287-0.293 m with nonzero arm velocity, not mandatory thresholds. Earlier aligned approach/close/lift transfer is possible to deliver_block because those phases overlap. Continue through incoming red release and retreat when the next intended source is blue; mere red goal alignment is not readiness for blue acquisition. These are skill guidance, not extra task success requirements.
limitations: Two causal observations and eight executed actions per replan are fixed, replacing the hypothesis's four observations and two actions. Latent attention replaces the unavailable explicit intent token and is not semantically supervised. Cannot reliably select blue first, resolve conflicting intent, or recover from unseen failures. No IK, FK, contact model, collision guarantee, rigid-motion equivariance, or arbitrary yaw generalization. Shared geometry may reduce coordinate memorization but absolute scene features and demonstrated order can still be memorized. Role-balanced resampling and auxiliary phase losses are not implemented; the original expanded training slices and shared full-demonstration normalizer are unchanged.

config.architecture: SharedRoleGeometry with conditional temporal U-Net epsilon denoiser
config.role_conditioning: Unlabelled scene-conditioned learned role queries; pose and matching world goal are kept bundled, without color or slot-position embeddings.
config.geometry_scaling: Common isotropic length = maximum frozen shared half-range over TCP/red/blue xyz; common world center = frozen TCP xyz mean. Robot qpos/qvel and TCP xyz use the provided shared per-channel affine normalization. No normalization is refitted.
config.loss: Masked mean squared epsilon error over normalized original actions; architectural prior_loss is zero.
config.slot_relabeling: Encoder is structurally invariant to exchanging the complete object pose-and-goal bundles across both history states; joint actions are not permuted or reflected. No extra consistency penalty.
config.sampling: Framework-provided unchanged slice-window batches; no custom role-balanced sampler or action selection.
config.segmentation: All 24 assigned expanded slices, stops exclusive; no phase filtering or shortened overlap.
